name: Barrio de los Artesanos
hero_subtitle: Living craft lanes of the medina — leather, textiles, metalwork and active workshops.

overview.title: Where crafts are still made
overview.p1: Tetouan's artisan quarter (and the craft streets of the medina) remains a place of active production. Leather, textiles, metalwork and other traditional skills are practised in small workshops rather than only sold as finished goods.
overview.p2: Walking these lanes is one of the best ways to see living heritage. Bargaining is expected in many shops; observing the work itself is often as rewarding as buying.
overview.p3: Morning is ideal — workshops are open, light is good, and the streets are less crowded than in the heat of the day.

tips.title: Practical tips for the Artisan Quarter

1.title: Morning is best
1.desc: Workshops are active, light is good, and temperatures are more comfortable.

2.title: Respectful shopping
2.desc: Bargain politely. Not every item is handmade on site — ask if it matters to you.

3.title: Photography
3.desc: Always ask before photographing people at work; many artisans are happy to be asked.

q1.question: Is there an entry fee?
q1.answer: No. The streets and most workshops are free to enter; you only pay for what you buy.

q2.question: How long should I stay?
q2.answer: One to two hours allows time to watch work, talk to artisans and shop without rushing.

q3.question: Is it suitable in summer?
q3.answer: Mornings are best. The lanes can be hot and busy later in the day.

q4.question: Do I need a guide?
q4.answer: Not required, but a good local guide can open workshop doors and explain techniques.

q5.question: Can I take photos of the work?
q5.answer: Usually yes if you ask first. Respect any refusal and avoid flash in small spaces.
